lessons.title: The Alphabet: Letters and Their Sounds
lessons.notes_html:
The Alphabet

This unit revises the alphabet. We learn the sound of every letter, capital and small letters, and pre-writing lines. English is written from left to right.

Say each letter sound aloud with its word: A/a apple, B/b bag, C/c cat, D/d dog, E/e egg, F/f fan, G/g goat, H/h hen, I/i ice cream, J/j jar, K/k kettle, L/l lion, M/m mango, N/n nest, O/o orange, P/p panda, Q/q queen, R/r ring, S/s star, T/t truck, U/u umbrella, V/v van, W/w whale, X/x x-ray, Y/y yolk, Z/z zebra.

Capital and Small Letters

Say the capital and small form of every letter together: Aa, Bb, Cc, Dd, Ee, Ff, Gg, Hh, Ii, Jj, Kk, Ll, Mm, Nn, Oo, Pp, Qq, Rr, Ss, Tt, Uu, Vv, Ww, Xx, Yy, Zz.

Name the pictures aloud: top, apple, fan, bed, football, orange, tree, snake.

Dialogue

Practise the Sara-Saad dialogue in pairs, smiling, nodding and keeping eye contact: Sara played on the swings with Fatima, and Saad played football with Ahmed and Zain. Saad invites Sara to join next time. This is oral work, so there is no written answer.

Key Points

There are 26 letters in the alphabet. Every letter has a capital form and a small form, and every letter has its own sound.

lessons.title: Letters Before and After
lessons.notes_html:
Before and After

Write what comes before and after the given letters.

  • Letter b: before a, after c.
  • Letter h: before g, after i.
  • Letter n: before m, after o.
  • Letter t: before s, after u.
  • Letter x: before w, after y.

Match Capital and Small Letters

Match each capital letter with its small letter: A-a, B-b, C-c, D-d, E-e, F-f, G-g, H-h, I-i, J-j, K-k, L-l, M-m, N-n, O-o, P-p, Q-q, R-r, S-s, T-t, U-u, V-v, W-w, X-x, Y-y, Z-z.

lessons.title: Rhyming Words
lessons.notes_html:
Rhyming Words

Rhyming words are words that have similar ending sounds.

  • -at: cat, hat, mat, sat, rat.
  • -ot: pot, dot, hot, got, lot.
  • -ap: cap, tap, map, lap, sap.
  • -op: top, mop, hop, pop, cop.
  • -an: can, fan, man, pan, van.

Key Points

Words that end with the same sound rhyme. Cat and hat rhyme because they both end with -at.

lessons.title: Commands and Requests
lessons.notes_html:
Commands and Requests

A command is an order to do something. A request is asking politely.

Commands: Sit down. Stand up. Raise your hand. Be quiet. Read your book. Close your book. Open your book. Knock at the door. Draw a picture. Open the door.

Requests: Please, close the door. Please, open your mouth.

Now do the actions: count your fingers, sit down, close the door, open your mouth, open your book. This is practical work, so there is no written answer.

Spell and Write the Words

bat, hat, mat, fan, was, man.

Key Points

A command tells us to do something. A request asks politely, and it often starts with Please.

lessons.title: Reading: A Zoo
lessons.notes_html:
The Reading

A zoo is a place where many animals and birds are kept in closed areas or cages. We can see lions, monkeys, elephants, parrots, snakes, and many other animals and birds in the zoo. People who take care of animals in the zoo are called zoo keepers. They give the animals food and water. We should not try to give anything to animals in the zoo. If we give anything to them, they may become ill and may die too. We should also keep a distance from them. Some animals and birds we keep at home, like hens, parrots and goats, are called pets, and we should take care of them at our homes.

Questions from the Reading

Q: Do you like animals and birds?
A: Model answer: Yes, I like animals and birds very much.

Q: What is your favourite animal or bird?
A: Model answer: My favourite animal is the lion. Write your own favourite.

Answer the Questions

Q: What is a zoo?
A: A zoo is a place where many animals and birds are kept in closed areas or cages.

Q: What animals and birds can we see in a zoo?
A: We can see lions, monkeys, elephants, parrots, snakes, and many other animals and birds in a zoo.

Q: Why shouldn't we feed the animals in a zoo?
A: We should not feed the animals in a zoo because if we give anything to them, they may become ill and may die too.

Choose the Correct Option

  • Where are animals and birds kept in a zoo? In cages or closed areas.
  • Who takes care of animals in the zoo? Zoo keepers.
  • What should we not do in the zoo? Give them food.
  • What can happen if we give food to animals in the zoo? They may get ill or die.
  • Which of these is a pet animal? Hen.

Dialogue: At the School Garden

Role-play as Ali, Sara and Teacher: Ali sees flowers, Sara sees a butterfly, the flowers are red and yellow, the leaf is green, and the bird is flying in the sky. This is oral work, so there is no written answer.

Key Points

A zoo keeps animals and birds in cages or closed areas. Zoo keepers feed them and take care of them. We must not feed zoo animals, because our food can make them ill.

Initial and Final Consonants

Words that start with a consonant: hand, bird; jar, jam; fan, frog; cup, clip; top, tag; bus, dress; gum, goat; van, vet; wash, brush; kite, kit; zoo, zip; rose, nose.

Words that end with a consonant: mat, man; buzz, jazz; bell, sell; sun, soap; car, bar; bop, top; x-ray, box; bath, math.

Alphabetical Order

Alphabetical order means writing letters or words in a, b, c order.

Examples: ball (b), dog (d), cat (c) go in the order b, c, d. House (h), fish (f), doll (d) go in the order d, f, h.

Beginning Letters in Alphabetical Order

  • Row 1: hen, sparrow, cage: c, h, s.
  • Row 2: pen, train, book: b, p, t.
  • Row 3: rabbit, crow, parrot: c, p, r.

Key Points

To put words in alphabetical order, look at the first letter of each word and arrange them from a to z.

lessons.title: Naming Words (Nouns)
lessons.notes_html:
Naming Words

A naming word is the name of a person, place or thing.

  • Persons: doctor, player, pilot, soldier.
  • Animals: cat, dog, cow, goat.
  • Places: school, hospital, park, zoo.
  • Things: bag, book, doll, cap.

Write the Naming Words in the Right Column

  • barber: Persons. policeman: Persons. teacher: Persons.
  • rabbit: Animals. elephant: Animals.
  • library: Places. zoo: Places. kitchen: Places.
  • fan: Things. clock: Things.

Use the Naming Words in Sentences

These are model sentences.

Q: teacher
A: Model sentence: My teacher is very kind.

Q: school
A: Model sentence: I go to school every day.

Q: fan
A: Model sentence: The fan is on the wall.

Q: tiger
A: Model sentence: The tiger is a big animal.

Q: pen
A: Model sentence: I write with my pen.

Rhyming Words

  • bat, hat.
  • mat, cat.
  • fan, man.
  • van, pan.

lessons.title: Short Vowel Sounds and Syllables

Short Vowel Sounds

The vowels are a, e, i, o, u.

  • i: ink, inch.
  • o: ox, orange.
  • u: up, umbrella.

One and Two Syllable Words

One syllable words are pronounced in one go and cannot be divided into parts, for example bed, jug. Two syllable words are pronounced in two parts, for example apple, table.

One syllable words: v _ n is van. b _ d is bed. j _ g is jug. d _ g is dog. c _ t is cat. c _ r is car.

Two syllable words: win _ _ ow is window. gar _ _ en is garden. bas _ _ et is basket. parr _ _ t is parrot. t _ _ ger is tiger.

Substitution Words

Substitution words are used in place of naming words. I, you, he, she, we, they and it are called substitution words.

Questioning Words

lessons.title: Reading: Cleanliness
lessons.notes_html:
The Reading

Cleanliness is a very important aspect of our lives. It helps to keep us healthy and free from diseases. We should know the importance of cleanliness and maintain good healthy habits. One of the most important things is to wash our hands with soap and water, especially before eating and after using the toilet. At school, we should keep our classroom clean and tidy by throwing garbage in the bin. We should also keep our desk clean by not writing anything on the desk or classroom walls. At home, we should make sure to put away our toys and belongings after playing, clean up any mess and help with household chores such as washing dishes or sweeping the floor. Taking a bath every day is also very important to keep our body clean and fresh. By maintaining good cleanliness habits, we can prevent the spread of germs and stay healthy. Let's make cleanliness a habit for life.

What Are the Kids Doing?

The kids in the pictures are: taking a bath, brushing their teeth, washing their hands, eating food, cleaning the park, and putting books in order on a shelf.

A: Cleanliness is very important because it helps to keep us healthy and free from diseases.

Q: When should we wash our hands?
A: We should wash our hands with soap and water, especially before eating and after using the toilet.

Q: How can we keep our classroom clean?
A: We can keep our classroom clean and tidy by throwing garbage in the bin, and by not writing anything on the desk or classroom walls.

Q: How can we prevent the spread of germs?
A: We can prevent the spread of germs by maintaining good cleanliness habits, such as washing our hands, taking a bath every day, and keeping our surroundings clean.

Q: How do you keep your home clean?
A: Model answer: I put away my toys after playing, clean up any mess, and help with household chores such as washing dishes and sweeping the floor.

  • When should we wash our hands? Before eating and after using the toilet.
  • Where should we throw garbage in the classroom? In the bin.
  • What should we do after playing at home? Put away our toys and clean up.

Conversation with Classmates

Practise the Bilal-Hinna dialogue in pairs: Hinna has a sandwich, Bilal has rice and an apple, and they eat together. This is oral work, so there is no written answer.

Key Points

lessons.title: Reading: The Story - The Bee and the Dove
lessons.notes_html:
The Story

Once upon a time, there was a bee which was very thirsty. It went to a stream to drink water. The flow of the water was very fast, so the bee fell into the stream, and its life was in danger. A dove was sitting on a branch of a nearby tree. It looked at the bee and dropped a leaf near the bee to save its life. The bee climbed up the leaf and saved its life. After some days, a hunter came and took aim at the dove. The bee was flying nearby. It looked at the hunter, so at once it flew near the hunter and stung his hand. The hunter missed the aim and the dove flew away. The dove thanked the bee for saving its life. The bee told the dove, "One day you saved my life, so it was my duty to help you in your difficult time."

Questions from the Story

Q: Did you like the story?
A: Model answer: Yes, I liked the story very much.

Q: How did the bee save the dove's life?
A: The bee flew near the hunter and stung his hand, so the hunter missed his aim and the dove flew away.

Q: What lesson did you learn from the story?
A: The lesson of the story is that we should help others in their difficult time. One good turn deserves another, because kindness is repaid with kindness.

Answer the Questions

Q: Who came to drink water at the stream?
A: A bee came to drink water at the stream.

Q: Which bird was sitting on the branch?
A: A dove was sitting on the branch of a nearby tree.

Q: What did the dove do to save the bee?
A: The dove dropped a leaf near the bee, and the bee climbed up the leaf and saved its life.

Q: Who aimed at the dove?
A: A hunter aimed at the dove.

Q: Why did the bee save the life of the dove?
A: Because the dove had saved the bee's life before, the bee felt it was its duty to help the dove in its difficult time.

Elements of a Story

There are three main elements of a story: 1. Beginning, 2. Middle, 3. Ending.

Tick the Correct Option

  • Why did the bee go to the stream? To drink water.
  • Who saved the bee from the stream? A dove.
  • What did the dove drop to save the bee? A leaf.
  • What did the hunter try to do? Shoot the dove.
  • How did the bee save the dove? By stinging the hunter.

Dialogue

Practise the Usman-Father dialogue in pairs: Usman asks his father to buy him a story book, and his father says he will buy one today. This is oral work, so there is no written answer.

Key Points

The dove saved the bee, and later the bee saved the dove. We should help others in their difficult time, because kindness is repaid with kindness.

lessons.title: Reading: Be Safe
lessons.notes_html:
The Reading

We all want to be safe at home, in school and outside. Being safe means we take care of ourselves. A stranger is a person we do not know. Strangers can be men, women or older children. We must never talk to a stranger. We must never go anywhere with a stranger. If someone we do not know calls us, we should walk away quickly. If a stranger asks for help, we should call an adult to help them. We should not help them alone. When we are outside, we should stay with our friends. We should walk on the sidewalk and stay away from the road. We should wait for our parents at the same place. If anyone offers us food, sweets, candy, toys or rides, we must say "No, thank you." We should never take anything from strangers. At home, we should not open the door to strangers. In school, we must follow our teacher's instructions. We should walk in a line, not run in the hall. We should play safely in the playground. When crossing the road, we always: Stop, look, then walk. If we ever feel scared or confused, we should ask our parents or teacher for help. Being safe means being smart. We should think before we act. We stay close to people we trust. We should take care of ourselves. When we follow safety rules, we can stay happy and safe.

Questions from the Reading

Q: When should we say "No" to strangers?
A: We should say "No, thank you" when a stranger offers us food, sweets, candy, toys or rides, and we should never take anything from strangers.

Q: How can we stay safe from strangers?
A: We stay safe by never talking to a stranger, never going anywhere with a stranger, walking away quickly if a stranger calls us, staying with our friends outside, and telling a trusted adult if we feel scared or uncomfortable.

Answer the Questions

Q: Who is a stranger?
A: A stranger is a person we do not know. Strangers can be men, women or older children.

Q: What should we do if a stranger offers us candy or toys?
A: We must say "No, thank you" and never take anything from a stranger.

Q: Who can we ask for help if we feel scared or confused?
A: We can ask our parents or teacher for help, or tell an adult we trust.

Q: What does being safe mean?
A: Being safe means we take care of ourselves: we think before we act, stay close to people we trust, and follow safety rules so we can stay happy and safe.

Fill in the Blanks

  • We should always remember not to talk to strangers or go with them.
  • We should also stay with our friends while playing outside.
  • We can always ask our parents or teachers if we have any questions about strangers.
  • We can help keep ourselves safe by being aware of our surroundings.

Dialogue

Practise the Laiba-Zara dialogue in pairs: Laiba has lost her pencil, and Zara gives her an extra pencil. This is oral work, so there is no written answer.

Key Points

Being safe means taking care of yourself. Never talk to a stranger, never go with a stranger, and never take anything from a stranger. When you cross the road, stop, look, then walk.
